approaches.name: Dynamic NSER social registry with multi-entry access and big data targeting
approaches.description: The project uses MELA access points, big data analytics, an updated PMT algorithm and a hybrid-scheme beneficiary registry to keep NSER household data current and targeting accurate. Practices: Multi-entry localized access (MELA) system for social registry updates; Big data analytics and updated PMT algorithm integrated into NSER targeting; Multi-entry localized access (MELA) registry intake system; Big data analytics and updated PMT algorithm for targeting; BISP digital platform tracking hybrid savings scheme accounts; Beneficiary registry platform for hybrid scheme linked to NSER; Big data assessment to complement NSER targeting methods; NADRA unique ID linking social registry data across systems; NSER data exchange interface with signed data sharing agreements; Beneficiary registry and platform for hybrid social protection scheme; IVR pilot for localized climate-disaster targeting; Beneficiary registry and MIS platform for hybrid SP scheme; NSER data exchange interface under signed data sharing agreements; Functional beneficiary registry and platform for hybrid SP scheme; MELA dynamic NSER data update mechanism; Hybrid scheme beneficiary registry and MIS platform; NSER interface integrating NDMA and Met hazard data; Geospatial and telecom big data to improve NSER targeting.

evidence.text: This includes the introduction of a multi-entry localized access (MELA) system that provides greater access to the social registry (NSER) to enable regular and timely updates, big data and analytics to improve targeting, and development of a hybrid SP scheme to gradually expand protection to the missing middle.

extra_evidence.text: Specifically, the program would: (i) Build-in greater innovation and technology within SP systems to improve the social registry’s capacity to maintain updated household data, exchange data with social programs, optimize use of cross- checks, improve data and analytics for targeting, and provide greater beneficiary choice in the biometric payment systems.
This RA will support, among others, the more frequent intake and registration for the social registry through introduction of a multi-entry, localized, access system.

The goal of the MELA mechanism is to (i) provide Page 10 of 50 The World Bank Pakistan Crisis-Resilient Social Protection (CRISP) (P174484) multiple points of entry (physical registration desks, door-to-door surveys, virtual services);
(ii) ensure that these access windows are local; and (iii) ensure that data flow is automated.
The Program will also support systematization of cross-checks and integration of big data and analytics into the social registry to enhance targeting performance.
The program will support systematization of cross-checks and integration of big data and analytics into the social registry to enhance targeting performance.

Combined methods have been shown to minimize errors.10 To increase beneficiary targeting accurancy, this RA will support more systematic use of data, and update of the Proxy Means Test (PMT) algorithm.

BISP will also develop a digital platform for tracking the hybrid scheme, which would include selection and enrollment status of beneficiaries, and information received from financial institutions on contributions, withdrawals, and shared profits of individual accounts.
The scheme will rely on existing institutional capacity and digital approaches for efficient delivery and promoting behavioral change.
This RA would also support operationalizing of the beneficiary registry (digital platform) for the hybrid scheme linked to NSER.
(ii) assessment of the effectiveness of use of big data to complement traditional targeting methods to improve targeting performance;
The linkage of the data across information systems is through the NADRA’s unique national identification system.
To ensure data quality and protection, BISP uses formal data sharing protocols for exchange between the social registry and other information systems.

approaches.name: Beneficiary-centric digital payments with competing payment service providers
approaches.description: The project pays safety net beneficiaries through a beneficiary-centric mechanism linked to the National Payment Gateway, letting them choose among competing payment service providers. Practices: Biometric payment system linked to National Payment Gateway; Beneficiary-centric digital payment mechanism with PSP choice and competition; Beneficiary-centric payment mechanism with PSP choice.
approaches.why_innovative: New delivery arrangement: gateway-linked biometric payments - cue: 'next generation' | category Financial; adoption apply; judged in 1 round(s); final check: digital core, in_use before 2019

evidence.text: It would also include the next generation of payment system reforms to link the BISP payment system to the National Payment Gateway.

extra_evidence.text: This RA will support advances in the biometric payment system, including technological innovations to promote greater financial inclusion and improvement in services.
This would make the payment system more beneficiary centric, remove redundancy of the payment systems, and build resilience against service disruptions from climate shocks.
